cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: The Greek Underworld (Hades) was the realm of the dead, ruled by the god Hades and his queen Persephone

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: All souls went to the Underworld — it was not simply a place of reward or punishment

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: Charon the ferryman transported souls across the River Styx — the dead were buried with a coin for payment

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: The Underworld had distinct regions: Asphodel Meadows for ordinary souls, Elysium for heroes, and Tartarus for the wicked

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: The three judges of the dead (Minos, Rhadamanthus and Aeacus) decided where souls would go

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: Persephone's abduction by Hades explained the seasons — she spent part of the year in the Underworld

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: Orpheus descended to the Underworld to retrieve his wife Eurydice but lost her by looking back

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: Theseus and Pirithous attempted to abduct Persephone but were trapped in chairs of forgetfulness

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: The River Lethe caused souls to forget their past lives before reincarnation in some traditions

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: Hermes psychopompos (guide of souls) escorted the dead to the Underworld

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: The Eleusinian Mysteries promised initiates a better afterlife, suggesting hope beyond mere existence in Asphodel

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of the Underworld
cards.back: Odysseus and Aeneas both visited the Underworld while still alive — katabasis or nekuia episodes
